document.title: Usama bin Ladin: U.S. Points Delivered to Taliban and Pakistani Government (Islamabad 04254)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan's Bin Laden Policy
document.note: [Secret] Taliban chargé d'affaires Syedur Rahman Haqqani calls bin Laden a bomb waiting to explode. U.S. officials grow frustrated with Pakistani and Taliban officials, who are courteous but expected to take little action. Pakistan says it is taking the bin Laden matter very seriously but is preoccupied with Indo-Pakistani tensions over Kashmir.

events.description: U.S. Ambassador delivered points on Bin Ladin to Taliban charge Haqqani; Haqqani promised to convey them to Mullah Omar.
Ambassador met Pakistani MFA official Murshed, who promised Pakistan would press the Taliban.
Planned visit of Uzbek FM Kamilov to Kandahar, with Pakistani officials possibly accompanying; next opportunity to raise issue with Taliban.
Mullah Jalil met Assistant Secretary Inderfurth.
Ambassador Milam reviewed U.S. points on bin Ladin with Taliban charge Haqqani; Haqqani promised to relay to Mullah Omar and Taliban foreign ministry.
Ambassador Milam met Pakistani MFA official Murshed, who promised Pakistan would press the Taliban over bin Ladin.
Mullah Jalil met Assistant Secretary Inderfurth (February meeting per refs).
Mullah Jalil met Charge d'Affaires Eastham (May meeting per refs).
Uzbek Foreign Minister Kamilov due to visit Kandahar, with Pakistani officials accompanying; seen as opportunity for Pakistan to press the Taliban.
Taliban removed bin Ladin's communications equipment after U.S. insistence; bin Ladin left Taliban-dominated territory.

key_claims: Taliban charge Haqqani claimed the Taliban had no idea where Bin Ladin was after removing his communications equipment.
Haqqani said Bin Ladin was like 'a bomb' because expelling him would provoke popular uprising against the Taliban.
The Taliban claimed to be quietly urging Bin Ladin to leave Afghanistan voluntarily.
Haqqani warned a third party might stage an incident to blame Bin Ladin and the Taliban.
The U.S. Ambassador said the U.S. had solid information that Bin Ladin was planning attacks and demanded immediate expulsion.
Pakistan's MFA promised to press the Taliban, with the Uzbek FM's Kandahar visit on 2 June 1999 as a possible opportunity.
